 Sports Luka Doncic came for revenge on Yaxel Lendeborg. The Warriors had other plans
 The Warriors completed their biggest comeback since 2015 by neutralizing the Lakers’ superstar’s playmaking.
 Steph Curry sent Luka Doncic to the floor before hitting a step-back 3-pointer on Friday at Chase Center. | Source: Ezra Shaw/Getty Images By Danny Emerman Sports Reporter Published Oct. 31, 2026 at 6 a.m. Share Share

 Close share menu There are 0 comments on this story Published Oct. 31, 2026 at 6 a.m. Yaxel Lendeborg didn’t just poke the bear in the Warriors’ season opener — he lobbed a flaming spear at it. 
 No one in Chase Center forgot about the rookie’s fiery debut, in which he told Lakers superstar Luka Doncic he sucks and said he lost all respect for him. Doncic certainly remembered. Amid “LUKA SUCKS” chants and boos every time he touched the ball, Doncic came out firing. He scored 21 points in the first quarter, stretching the Lakers’ lead to a shell-shocking 25 points.
 But the Warriors had Lendeborg’s back. They turned Doncic into a one-on-one player and went right at him on offense. Doncic dished five assists in his first 12 minutes and none in his next 25. Lendeborg took a second-round knockout, but the Warriors picked him up off the mat. 
 ADVERTISEMENT
 As Doncic seemingly vied to single-handedly get his revenge on the Warriors, Golden State used a holistic, selfless, connected approach to secure a stunning 112-95 victory. 
 The Warriors (3-3) pulled off their biggest comeback since 2015 for their third straight win. Their bench outscored the Lakers’ 50-7 . The Warriors threw a variety of defensive looks at Doncic, neutralizing his playmaking and rendering him inefficient after his blazing start. Steph Curry relentlessly attacked Doncic on switches, including when he dropped him to the blue NBA Cup court for a step-back 3. The Warriors’ defense, led by Draymond Green, held one of the most potent offenses in the league to 15 points in each of the second and fourth quarters. 
 Lendeborg got in his own head before a matchup he had hyped himself, but the Warriors made his first career stinker easier to stomach by winning.  
 “That’s part of it, for sure — have your brother’s back,” Curry said.
 Doncic, the league’s leading scorer, finished with 37 points. Golden State looked shaken early, turning it over 10 times in the first 10 minutes. Doncic paced the Lakers to a 25-point lead as he shushed the crowd and blew kisses after 3-pointers. 
 “I think they came out the gates with the hype from last game and all the talk that was going on, you could tell they were feeding into that,” De’Anthony Melton said. “And they wanted to try to punch us in our mouth, try to teach us a lesson, whatever it was. But after we got punched, we responded.” 
 The Warriors’ energy flipped in the huddle between the first and second quarters, sparked by motivational words from assistant coach Anthony Vereen. 
 As Doncic sat to start the second quarter, the Warriors chipped away. Melton flew around and hit 3s. Charles Bassey came out of nowhere for a block that led to a Lendeborg alley-oop. The Warriors’ bench trimmed the deficit to single digits. 
 Then, Curry returned and led an 18-4 run to close the half. The Warriors lost the first quarter 38-15 as Doncic took on the world. They won the second quarter 38-15 as they cleaned up their turnovers and applied more ball pressure to the six-time All-Star. 
 Lendeborg started on Doncic, but foul trouble mostly removed him from the matchup. Green took a turn. Brandin Podziemski — who put together his fourth straight excellent game — got back-to-back stops on Doncic to end the half. Golden State sent traps at Doncic to get the ball out of his hands, picked him up full-court, and stayed disciplined in help defense to prevent the type of lobs to Walker Kessler that destroyed them in the season opener.

 Doncic made 1 of 5 shots in the second quarter after completely controlling the opening frame.
 “Luka had an unbelievable first quarter,” Curry said. “He looked very determined coming into the night.” 
 Doncic, the all-time leader in usage rate (39.8%), took 27 shots as the Warriors’ defense turned him into an isolation scorer. 
 The Warriors’ offense helped their defense, too. They turned it over only five times after the first quarter, preventing the type of  transition chances Doncic thrives on.

 They also made a point of making Doncic work defensively. Whenever Curry got Doncic on a switch, he attacked.
 Curry held his hands over the sides of his head in faux disbelief after dropping Doncic with a step-back. After drilling a fadeaway in the corner over Doncic, he did maraca hands. He even invented a new animated gesture.  (opens in new tab) 
 The bear had already been poked. Curry tranquilized it. 
 Curry’s expressiveness took the spotlight away from Lendeborg and put it right on himself, all while tiring Doncic and demoralizing the Lakers. 
 Curry finished with 31 points. Podziemski added 21, a drawn charge, and myriad winning plays. Georges Niang hit three 3-pointers, Melton dropped 16 points, Green dished nine assists, and Will Richard played tenacious on-ball defense. 
 Meanwhile, Doncic was on an island. The Warriors goaded his co-star, Austin Reaves, into eight turnovers and took away his favorite lob target, Kessler. No other Laker made an impact. 
 “The way he started that first quarter was ridiculous,” Curry said. “And it was going to require everybody to be a little more physical, a little more connected, and kind of withstand his flurries that he had. Of course, that’s backing Yaxel up, and that’s the collective energy that we need to win this game.” 
 From the end of the third quarter to the start of the fourth, the Warriors outscored the Lakers 26-4. Their 17-point win is the largest margin of victory for a team that trailed by 25 or more in the play-by-play era. Curry heard ‘MVP’ chants after passing Dominique Wilkins for 18th on the all-time scoring list, and Doncic got the wrong end of the highlight reel. 
 And Lendeborg received another learning experience. 
 “Them boys had my back today,” Lendeborg said. “It was amazing to see. Steph Curry, again, did his thing.”
